message.content:
Critics of Nicolaus Copernicus included conservative astronomers, theologians, and Aristotelian philosophers who defended the geocentric Ptolemaic model.
Who among them challenged his sun-centered cosmos?
What a bold challenge his theory presented!
Tycho Brahe later rejected a fully heliocentric system, though he valued Copernicus's mathematical elegance.
Did Brahe attack Copernicus personally, or only his cosmology?
How fascinating that blend of respect and rejection was!
Christopher Clavius, a Jesuit mathematician, defended the older astronomical system against Copernican alternatives.
What did Clavius find most problematic in Copernicus's work?
How firmly tradition still anchored his judgment!
Some Church authorities worried that heliocentrism could undermine a literal reading of Scripture.
Which specific passages made them uneasy?
What tension arose between science and theology!
